title: The Sample Space: Edge 2-Colorings of K_n
content: `Edges n` is the set of 2-element subsets of Fin n — the edges of the complete graph K_n — and `Coloring n := Edges n → Bool` assigns each edge one of two colors. `card_Edges` proves there are exactly C(n,2) edges (via Finset.card_powersetCard), so the sample space has 2^(C(n,2)) colorings. Modeling colorings as honest functions on the 2-subsets, rather than an abstract placeholder, is what lets the first-moment count be carried out concretely over ℕ.

title: Induced Clique Edges and Monochromatic Cliques
content: `EdgesIn n K` collects the edges contained in a vertex set K. `card_EdgesIn` proves these biject with the 2-subsets of K — the image under the coercion to Finset (Fin n) equals K.powersetCard 2 — so a k-clique has exactly C(k,2) induced edges. `Mono c K` is the event that all of K's induced edges share one color (with a Decidable instance, used for the concrete n=6 case). These are the cliques the union bound will count over.

title: The Crux Count via an Explicit Injection
content: `card_mono_le` is the heart of the first-moment estimate: the colorings monochromatic on a fixed clique K (with at least one edge) number at most 2·2^(C(n,2) − |EdgesIn K|). The proof builds an explicit injection ψ from such colorings into Bool × (off-clique edges → Bool): a monochromatic coloring is fully recovered from its single common color on the clique (read at any edge e₀) together with its values on every edge OUTSIDE the clique. Injectivity is checked edge-by-edge (on-clique edges all equal the common color; off-clique edges agree directly), and Fintype.card_le_of_injective plus the product/function cardinalities give the bound. This 'constant on a sub-family of coordinates ⟹ ≤ 2·2^(N−|family|)' lemma is a reusable union-bound tool.

title: The Union Bound: Bad Colorings Cannot Exhaust the Space
content: `first_moment_ramsey` assembles the bound. The 'bad' colorings (monochromatic on SOME k-clique) form a biUnion over the C(n,k) cliques; `Finset.card_biUnion_le` plus card_mono_le bounds |Bad| by C(n,k)·2·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) = (2·C(n,k))·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)). Splitting the total 2^(C(n,2)) = 2^(C(k,2))·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) (using C(k,2) ≤ C(n,2) from Nat.choose_le_choose) and applying the hypothesis 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) shows |Bad| < total. Hence some coloring is not bad — and it has no monochromatic K_k. This is Erdős's 'expected count < 1 ⟹ a beating-the-average object exists', rendered as pure ℕ counting with no measure.

title: R(k,k) > n and the Concrete Witness R(4,4) > 6
content: `ramsey_number_gt` restates the bound in the standard Ramsey form — there is a coloring in which every k-clique contains two differently-colored edges (no monochromatic K_k), so the diagonal Ramsey number satisfies R(k,k) > n. `ramsey_four_gt_six` instantiates k=4, n=6: 2·C(6,4) = 30 < 64 = 2^(C(4,2)) is checked by decide, giving R(4,4) > 6 (a 2-coloring of K_6 with no monochromatic K_4). This confirms the hypothesis is satisfiable and the bound non-vacuous — while remaining axiom-free, since decide uses kernel reduction (not native_decide).
